name: merchants-affected-by-fee
pattern: (which merchants would have been affected|which merchants were affected by the fee)
operation: the merchants with at least one transaction matching a rule (or losing it under a change)
invariant: affected ⊆ merchants matching the rule today

canonical_method.helper: transactions_matching_rule(transactions, rule_id) then filter by the new restriction
steps: txns = transactions_matching_rule(payments_period, rule_id) — this is 'merchants matching the rule today', satisfying the stated invariant
affected = [m for m in today_merchants if get_merchant_info(m)[<changed field>] != <new restricted value>]
sort and comma-join; empty string if none

conflict_ruling: task 2571 computes today's matching merchant set via transactions_matching_rule first, then filters by account_type — this correctly grounds the answer in actual matching transactions and satisfies affected⊆merchants-matching-rule-today. Task 2555 instead reasons from the static full merchant list's account_type without first confirming those merchants had matching transactions this period, which can overcount if a merchant qualifies by account_type but never actually triggered the rule.
pitfalls: Filtering by merchant's static account_type alone (2555) instead of first restricting to transactions_matching_rule's actual matching set can add merchants who never triggered the original rule
2 of 3 probe tasks (2571, 2557) disagreed between passes — self-consistency is not yet reliable in this family
prompt_rule: if the question asks which merchants would be affected by narrowing a fee rule's criteria → transactions_matching_rule(payments_period, rule_id) to get today's matching merchants, then filter out those still matching the narrowed criteria; format: comma-separated sorted merchant names, empty string if none.
note: No dev-10 anchor; needs one before promotion given the self-agreement failures.
